anomalies.description: A large, sudden explosion erupts from the lower-left side of a multi-story building, producing a rapidly expanding fireball and a dense plume of black smoke; the blast appears to be a controlled demolition or accidental detonation.

A large, sustained fireball erupts from the left side of a multi-story building, rapidly expanding upward and across multiple floors, accompanied by thick black smoke—indicative of a high-energy explosion followed by intense combustion.

A large, sudden fireball erupts from the left side of the building, rapidly expanding and producing a massive plume of black smoke—characteristic of a violent explosion or deflagration event.; A secondary, upward-propagating explosive fire front ignites along the upper facade, spreading rapidly across multiple floors—indicative of a continuing explosive event (e.g., flashover or sequential detonation of flammable materials).

A controlled demolition explosion occurs: the building's left side collapses inward and downward, generating a massive dust cloud that rapidly engulfs the lower portion of the structure; the upper right section remains momentarily standing before beginning to tilt.

Controlled demolition of a multi-story building via explosive charges, resulting in rapid progressive collapse from the base upward, with massive dust cloud and black smoke plume.; Mechanical demolition using heavy excavator equipment; visible arm impact and structural failure of a smaller building, generating localized dust but no blast wave or smoke indicative of explosives.
